scope: Independent static review of isolated deterministic bounded whole-unit batch memoization; no production edits, compilation, test execution or performance acceptance by reviewer.
verdict: No source-level correctness blocker found in the reviewed snapshot. Runtime gates remain pending.
checked_invariants: Program rules/source/order are borrowed immutably. Each worker calls unchanged plain native reduce with the exact same target and reduction limits. No descendant-tail replacement or within-reduction queue change.

Coordinator holds the memo mutex across planning, native work and ordered commit. Cache hit/recency/insertion/eviction follows input order, giving an induction against a serial caller that continues through all Result values.

Planned duplicate misses share at most the first prefetched result. A later real miss reexecutes if the first result was uncacheable or evicted. Snapshot hits evicted before their turn also reexecute.

Whole native result includes exact terminal and unresolved coefficients, ordered conditions, non-NoRule failures and logical application counts. Existing memo refuses non-NoRule results, preserving failure evidence.

Batch is explicitly non-fail-fast. All per-item native or codec errors remain errors; later independent work may already have executed. Caller must inspect each item and account actual batch work even if it stops logical consumption early.
Actual known applications include every native Ok result; native Err sets an explicit incomplete-count flag. Returned logical, cached and uncached application totals remain distinct.

Pool-construction and input-bound errors precede native work/cache mutation. Pool size and input window bound simultaneous whole reductions and staged count, not total CAS threads, scratch memory, returned decoded coefficients or latency.
Native lifecycle and prior memo implementation differ only by batch module/reexports; no existing serial/ordinary API behavior is changed.

resource_and_state_qualification: No cancellation poll is added inside plain native reduction. Native-call and decode/CAS latency remain inherited.
